questions.q: In a shadow deployment, what happens to the new model's prediction?
options: It is always returned to the user instead of the production model's prediction
It is logged for comparison but never returned to the user — the production model's response is the only one the user sees
It replaces the production model immediately
It is averaged together with the production model's prediction
questions.explain: Shadowing mirrors live traffic to the new model purely for observation; its output is discarded from the user's perspective, making it zero-risk.

questions.q: In the Istio VirtualService canary example with weight 95/5, what actually happens to the 5%?
options: Those requests are dropped entirely
Those requests are genuinely served by the new model version, and real users receive and act on its predictions
Those requests are logged but discarded, like a shadow deployment
Those requests are sent to both versions simultaneously
questions.explain: Unlike shadow mode, a canary's traffic split is real: the percentage routed to the new version is actually served by it, with real consequences.

questions.q: Why would a team run a shadow deployment before a canary deployment, rather than going straight to canary?
options: Shadow mode is required by Kubernetes before any canary can run
Shadow mode validates latency and gross prediction behavior on real traffic with zero user-facing risk, before exposing any real users
Shadow deployments are faster to set up than canaries
Canary deployments cannot use Istio
questions.explain: Shadowing lets a team catch major issues with zero risk first; only once that looks clean does it make sense to expose real users via a canary.

questions.q: Why is watching only error rate and infrastructure health insufficient for a canary gate?
options: Error rate cannot be measured by Istio
A model can be fully healthy from an infrastructure standpoint while its predictions quietly regress for a specific customer segment
Error rate is only relevant for shadow deployments
Canaries never produce errors
questions.explain: A canary that returns 200s and looks fine in aggregate can still be worse for one segment, or have a shifted output-score distribution — a thorough gate checks prediction-level and segment-level signals too.

questions.q: What does the `mirror` field do in an Istio VirtualService?
options: It duplicates a request to a second destination without affecting the response returned to the client
It encrypts traffic between two services
It load-balances traffic evenly across all available replicas
It caches the response for faster subsequent requests
questions.explain: mirror is the mechanism behind shadow deployments: it sends a copy of the request to another destination while the real response still comes from the primary route.
